beforeCard.prompt: Какой морской парк у побережья Квинсленда охраняет крупнейшую в мире систему коралловых рифов?

answers.note: Управление им осуществляет Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority — государственное агентство Австралии.
Какаду — австралийский парк с водно-болотными угодьями и древним наскальным искусством аборигенов.
Улуру — Ката-Тьюта охраняет красный монолит Улуру и купола Ката-Тьюта в центре Австралии.
Фьордленд — новозеландский парк с фьордами Милфорд-Саунд и Даутфул-Саунд.

independentDefects.field: ordered answer labels and distractor set
independentDefects.finding: Actual current prompt restricts answer to a marine park off Queensland protecting a coral-reef system. Correct label alone fully repeats морской парк and риф, whereas three alternatives are bare national-park names. This is not a suffix/length-only rejection: full primary contexts show Uluru–Kata Tjuta is a red-sand, inland central-Australian desert/monolith park far from coastal cities (UNESCO L5,L52-L54), so it gives no credible marine/coral confusion in this exact question. Kakadu has real tidal/coastal wetlands (UNESCO L5,L46,L52) and Fiordland has actual marine reserves/fjords (DOC MilfordL18 and DoubtfulL16), so these two are not rejected merely as land parks; nevertheless the complete set lacks three plausible competing marine-reef protected areas, and its sole explicit marine/reef label offers a strong category shortcut before comparing facts.

rule.requirement: Four plausible options in actual context, comparable category/detail, no answer giveaway through presentation or obviously impossible distractor.
rule.interpretation: Applied to verified actual environment and current complete wording, not an automatic ban on official marine-park prefixes or unequal proper-name lengths.
